name: Mount Washington Auto Road
unique: A 7.6 mile road climbing 4,618 feet to the summit of the highest peak in the northeast, where the weather is measured in hurricane force and the view runs to Canada.
buzz: The drive is narrow with no guardrails and the summit is 30 degrees colder; check the summit forecast, they close the road for wind.

name: Santa's Village
unique: A 1950s Christmas theme park in the White Mountains with a reindeer herd, a train through the woods and a bakery that sells gingerbread all summer.
buzz: Parents call it the cleanest small park they have visited; children under eight are the right age and the reindeer are real.

name: Flume Gorge
unique: A boardwalk through a 90 foot granite chasm with waterfalls on both walls, discovered in 1808 and still the most visited natural site in the White Mountains.
buzz: The boardwalk is steep in places and the loop takes 90 minutes; go before nine to beat the tour buses.

name: Clark's Bears
unique: A 1928 family park with a steam train that climbs a trestle, a water blaster boat ride and trained bears performing in a ring, run by the same family for four generations.
buzz: The train and the bear show are the tradition and both feel like 1965 in a good way; teenagers may be bored and small children are not.

name: Lost River Gorge
unique: A boardwalk and boulder cave route through a gorge where the river disappears underground, with crawl spaces named after what they do to your knees.
buzz: Children love the caves and adults find the boardwalk sections slick; wear shoes that can get wet and skip the caves if you are claustrophobic.

name: Hampton Beach Boardwalk
unique: A old fashioned seaside strip of fried dough, arcades, a bandshell and a wide sand beach, with the state's biggest free summer fireworks on Wednesdays.
buzz: It is loud and crowded and that is the point; parking is the hassle and the north beach is quieter.

name: Fuller Gardens
unique: A formal rose garden and Japanese garden behind a 1900s summer estate, a mile from the ocean in a town of 4,500.
buzz: Rose people come in late June and the Japanese garden is the quiet corner; it is small and the admission is modest.

name: Castle in the Clouds
customer: House tour people, hikers, leaf peepers
unique: A 1914 Arts and Crafts mansion on a mountain above Lake Winnipesaukee, with a working farm, carriage roads and a waterfall trail on 5,000 acres.
buzz: The view from the terrace is the reason to come and the trails are the surprise; the house tour is timed and the drive up is steep.

name: MS Mount Washington
unique: A 230 foot excursion boat that circles Lake Winnipesaukee past 365 islands, with a view of the Ossipee and Belknap ranges from the top deck.
buzz: The Sunday brunch cruise is the local tradition and the top deck is worth the wind; the lake is 20 miles long and the trip covers a fraction.

name: Gunstock Mountain
unique: A ski hill with a view of Lake Winnipesaukee from every run, plus a summer adventure park with a mountain coaster and an aerial treetop course.
buzz: Families like the smaller scale and the lake view; the terrain is not steep and the lodge is old but the snowmaking is serious.

name: Conway Scenic Railroad
unique: A 1870s railroad running steam and diesel excursions through Crawford Notch, with a climb up the Frankenstein Trestle and a view of Mount Washington.
buzz: The Notch train is the scenic one and the valley train is the short one; book the dome car for fall and sit on the left going up.

name: Story Land
unique: A nursery rhyme theme park in the White Mountains with a wooden coaster, a pirate ship and a pumpkin coach, scaled for small children and shaded by real trees.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for a first park and the lines are short before noon; teenagers will be bored by two.

name: Diana's Baths
unique: A series of ledge pools and small waterfalls on Lucy Brook where the water has cut potholes into the granite, a half mile walk from the road.
buzz: The lower falls are crowded and the upper pools are quieter; the rocks are slippery and the water is cold even in August.

name: Mount Monadnock
unique: A bare granite summit above the treeline with a 100 mile view, reached by a 1.8 mile trail that is one of the most climbed mountains in the world.
buzz: The White Dot trail is steep and exposed and the summit is windy; start early, the parking lot fills by nine on weekends.

name: Keene Pumpkin Festival
unique: A downtown festival where thousands of carved jack o'lanterns are stacked into towers and lit at once, a record setting attempt that started as a local fundraiser.
buzz: The towers at dusk are the spectacle; the event has had crowd troubles in the past and now runs with tighter security and shuttles.

name: Madame Sherri Forest
company: Society for the Protection of New Hampshire Forests
unique: The stone staircase and foundations of a costume designer's castle in the woods, with a trail to a swimming pond and an old quarry.
buzz: The staircase is the photograph everyone takes; the trail is short and the pond is a local swimming hole in summer.

name: Currier Museum of Art
unique: A small museum with a Wyeth, a Picasso and a Monet, plus tours of two Frank Lloyd Wright houses a few miles away.
buzz: The Wright house tour is the reason to book ahead; the museum itself is calm and the collection is better than a city this size suggests.

name: Milford Drive-In
unique: A two screen drive-in in the woods north of Nashua, with a playground under the screen and double features that run past midnight.
buzz: Cash only at the snack bar and the early show fills; bring a battery radio if your car stereo is not great.

name: McAuliffe-Shepard Discovery Center
unique: A planetarium and science center named for the teacher who died on Challenger and the first American in space, with a Mercury capsule and a full dome theater.
buzz: The planetarium shows are the draw and the exhibits are best for ages six to twelve; the building is next to the state technical college.

name: Canterbury Shaker Village
unique: Twenty five original Shaker buildings on a hilltop, with a meetinghouse, a laundry, gardens and demonstrations of the inventions the community patented.
buzz: The guides are excellent and the village is quiet; the Shaker furniture and the round barn are the highlights.

name: Woodman Institute Museum
unique: Four buildings on a Dover block holding a mineral collection, a taxidermy hall, a colonial garrison house and a 1675 settler's home with a bullet hole in the door.
buzz: The garrison house and the odd collections are the charm; it is volunteer run and feels like a museum from 1950.

name: Children's Museum of New Hampshire
unique: A hands on museum in a 1904 armory with a working post office, a lobster boat and a maker space where children build and test things.
buzz: Parents say the age range is two to eight and the maker space is the reason older siblings agree to come; it is quiet on weekday afternoons.

name: Saint-Gaudens National Historical Park
unique: The sculptor's home and studio with the original plaster of the Shaw memorial, a colonnade he built for his casts and a garden that looks across the Connecticut River.
buzz: Sculpture people call it a pilgrimage and the outdoor casts are the reason; the summer concert series on the lawn is the local event.

name: Mount Sunapee
unique: A ski mountain inside a state park with a view of Lake Sunapee from the summit and a beginner area that is genuinely separate from the expert runs.
buzz: Families like the layout and the lodge; the summit chair is the scenic ride in fall and the state beach is across the road.

name: Fort at No. 4
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: A reconstructed palisade fort and village on the Connecticut River where settlers held out during King George's War, with period gardens and livestock.
buzz: The reenactment weekends are the time to go; on ordinary days the fort is quiet and the guides have time to talk.
